author: volunteer state news
title: Memphis Tigers softball to end regular season with series at Wichita State
text:
The University of Memphis softball team will conclude its regular season with a three-game series against the Wichita State Shockers, who have won 11 of their last 12 conference games, according to an April 29 announcement. The games are scheduled for Thursday and Friday at 6 p.m., and Saturday at noon, all in Central Time. Each game will be broadcast on ESPN+.
This series marks the final opportunity for Memphis (18-35, 6-18 American) to build momentum before postseason play. The Tigers recently achieved their first-ever win over Florida Atlantic thanks to a walk-off two-run home run. A key player has led the team in batting average (.387), OPS (1.126), hits (55), runs (33), doubles (11), and walks (20). She was recognized as an honorable mention by the American Conference earlier this week. Another player continues to lead Memphis in home runs (8) and RBI (37); her RBI total ties for fourth-most in a single season for the program.
Freshman pitcher Stutts has been notable this year, securing her seventh win during the victory over Florida Atlantic. She leads Memphis pitchers in earned run average (5.48), innings pitched (107.1), strikeouts (51), and saves (2). Other pitchers have contributed around or above 50 innings each this season, with some maintaining sub-4.00 ERAs.
Wichita State enters the matchup with a record of 32-16 overall and an 18-6 mark in conference play after a recent loss at Kansas. Their offense is led by Ausha Moore, who has hit 20 home runs and driven in 51 runs as a sophomore transfer from North Texas, while Kinzey Woody is hitting above .350 with significant extra-base hits and was named to the NFCA Freshman of the Year Top 25 Watchlist last week.
On defense, sophomore Ryley Nihart leads Wichita State’s pitching staff with nearly half of their total innings pitched this season; Jade Sanders was recently named American Conference Pitcher of the Week after throwing scoreless innings against North Texas.
In head-to-head matchups since 2010, Memphis holds four wins compared to Wichita State’s twenty-one victories. Last year’s series also took place on the final weekend of regular play; it included one Memphis win that ended a long losing streak against Wichita State.
